parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes a universal traveller-facing document exposure: the national passport regime processes only birth-sex markers, officers are instructed to refuse and investigate suspected sex discrepancies, with a fraud misrepresentation ground carrying lifetime ineligibility, and foreign governments have issued travel advisories after documented detentions of visitors. Custody in national immigration detention is documented as abusive for trans people. The division sits in the 'Worst Policies In Effect' tier: a misdemeanour for trans facility use where a minor is present, a K-12 facility ban, an enforced (litigation ongoing) minor care ban, no state hate-crime or gender-identity discrimination protection, and licensed religious refusal of healthcare. Countervailing but partial: courts have enjoined several national orders, national hate-crime law and employment protections exist, no sodomy law, and most facility/presentation space is unregulated. Consequences centre on denial, detention risk and criminal exposure rather than routine imprisonment, keeping this above the severe band but below unremedied-exposure-only 0.45 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport X processing ended; case-note tag directs refusal and further inquiry on suspected sex discrepancy; fraud ground permits permanent ineligibility; passports confiscated/blocked and visitors stranded; foreign advisories issued after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Waiver possibility on fraud finding; national courts still reviewing the marker policy; existing X passports valid until expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: Document suspicion at a visa post or checkpoint can cascade into refusal, investigation and denial of entry before any state rule applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented detentions of foreign citizens over visa/document issues; national immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse of trans detainees; corrections bureau adopts hormone-withdrawal and conversion-style policies.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National courts have enjoined several executive orders; but supervision findings recur without remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An entry discrepancy investigation can lead straight to detention under a birth-sex-custody national regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division misdemeanour for trans use of facilities where a minor is present (intent element) plus extended K-12 ban; ~19 national subunits restrict facilities in government buildings; 4 criminalise in certain circumstances; state law defines sex restrictively.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented at division level; some regions nationally have no ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exposure is enforced by state/local officers and escalates via trespass; travel with a minor raises the misdemeanour trigger.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors (enforced after appeals reversal, litigation continuing); religious-refusal statute; 15-year provider liability; national push to bar under-18 reimbursement; hospital record subpoenas.
care_services.protection: National judge earlier enjoined ban for irreparable harm; litigation unresolved.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor cannot access care in the division; an adult's refill/eemergency care may be refused on belief grounds.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders frame trans identities as ideology, anti-trans terrorist-prioritisation language, healthcare framed as 'mutilation'; majority public support for assigned-sex documents; division placed worst-policy tier.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts rejecting some framing in litigation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level threat framing justifies facility and care restrictions officials actively enforce.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor: care ban enforceable, teacher/social-transition prosecutions directed nationally, K-12 facility exclusion, sports ban; guardian faces misdemeanour-facility exposure with a child present.
minors_guardians.protection: Care-ban injunctions partially contested; most protection avenues unremedied.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor-related restrictions convert ordinary guardianship into potential investigation exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Only documented arrest occurred in another subunit; division has no hate-crime enhancement; police response uneven nationally.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute since 2009; some subunits have bias statutes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local arrest for facility use feeds into a criminal system lacking identity-based protections.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforceability of care ban and Act 619 enforcement record unresolved; extent of facility ban beyond schools unclear in division.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ongoing national litigation; civil-liberties challenges and legal-aid FAQ maintain contested but functioning court channels.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty compounds risk: traveller cannot predict which regime is operative at travel time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both feature universal birth-sex facility rules and unremedied exposure. Here exposure additionally spans entry documents (fraud ground, detentions of visitors) and abusive custody, which 0.35-A lacks — so the case is materially lower than 0.35-A.

0.45-A has one polite but enforced birth-sex rule and otherwise working institutions. This jurisdiction layers entry-level universal exposure, documented visitor detentions, a worst-tier division and minor care ban onto that pattern, pushing below 0.45-A.

0.75-C shows dead-letter law, accepted documents and enforced remedies. Here laws are actively enforced against visitors at borders and in custody, and no division-level remedy exists for facilities or discrimination — far below.

0.15-D involves a registry driving near-systematic detention, extortion and imprisonment. This regime's exposures are entry-document and facility-focused with litigation channels partially operating and no documented routine imprisonment of visitors — well above 0.15-D.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a national document apparatus that screens every visitor for sex-at-birth consistency (marker refusal, investigation tags, fraud-based lifetime bans) with a division sitting in the worst policy tier: misdemeanour facility use, enforced minor care ban, no state protections, and licensed care refusal. The worst documented chain — a discrepant document triggers investigation, denial or detention into a hostile custody system — is a tier-1/2 exposure reaching every trans traveller at entry. Working but partial courts (injunctions, pending suits), national hate-crime law and marriage recognition are real mitigations, preventing classification as severe risk; but the combined operative rules reach every checkpoint and any travel involving a minor, keeping the jurisdiction in the upper high-risk band.
